name: Keycloak
description: Keycloak 26.7.3 container image at its defaults. Build record: what the image does before anyone deploys it.
comment: NON-CONFORMING EXAMPLE. The product record with the key types the Admin REST API can generate left out. Fails pqc-migration-extended#I3 only: the operator cannot tell whether the key management surface can create an ML-DSA key.

attributes.name: negotiationControl
values: Named groups are set by the JVM property jdk.tls.namedGroups

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Server certificate and key are operator-supplied files. Carries the HTTPS service, and through it OIDC, SAML and the Admin API.

attributes.name: negotiationControl
values: Inherits the main listener TLS settings by default

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Health and metrics only; the services it carries apply no cryptography of their own and are not declared separately (K7)

attributes.name: negotiationControl
values: TLS mode set in the JDBC URL

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Driver default is opportunistic TLS without verification

interfaces.name: TLS to the directory (LDAPS or StartTLS)

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Directory server must also support the new groups

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Carries the brokered token verification service

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Mail server must also support the new groups

attributes.name: negotiationControl
values: Not configurable beyond the JVM named groups

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Certificate is product-generated RSA-2048, rotated every 30 days

attributes.name: negotiationControl
values: Signature algorithm is set per realm (defaultSignatureAlgorithm) and per client

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: ML-DSA-65 signed tokens exceed the 4 KB browser cookie limit; relying parties must accept the AKP JWK key type, which is still an Internet-Draft

attributes.name: negotiationControl
values: Signature algorithm is set per client

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: No ML-DSA identifiers are standardised for XML Signature

interfaces.name: HTTP listener (plaintext; off by default in production mode)

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Carries tokens and credentials in clear on the proxy hop

interfaces.name: Admin REST API and Admin Console (bearer tokens)
Brokered token verification (external OIDC and SAML providers)

attributes.name: negotiationControl
values: Accepted algorithms set per identity provider

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: The external provider chooses the signature algorithm; Keycloak can accept ML-DSA only once it can verify it

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Key material held in the database in plaintext (#39933)

rules.text: Every interface it applies to states keyTypesSupported
rules.note: The key types the surface can generate or import, as algorithm names under the inherited scheme. This is the rule with the most value at this depth. The case it catches is ordinary: a TLS listener supports ML-DSA certificates and the product's key tool cannot create the key. Every baseline rule passes and the operator still cannot migrate. cprofile has no field for it.
